krishna_summary: Reliance is India's largest conglomerate spanning oil refining, petrochemicals, retail stores, and Jio telecom services.
The stock has dropped over 21% in the past year, hovering near its lowest price level of the year.
While Jio telecom profits are growing rapidly, the core oil-to-chemicals refining business is dragging down overall corporate profits.
Watch whether the stock holds its yearly low or starts climbing back above its recent average prices.
hanuman_section: Jio Platforms delivered robust profit growth of 23.4% YoY to ₹6,536 crore, boosted by telecom tariff hikes lifting ARPU to ₹195.1.
The stock trades at a discounted P/E of 19.2x to 21.4x compared to its five-year historical average of ~25.4x.
MACD has crossed above its signal line, revealing emerging positive short-term momentum despite the prevailing downtrend.
Digital Services demonstrated strong operational profitability with an EBITDA margin of 49.7%.
vibhishana_section: O2C segment EBITDA plunged 23.7% YoY to ₹12,413 crore due to weak chemical margins and lower fuel cracks, hurting consolidated net profit.
Derivatives positioning shows active short build-up with a bearish bias of -46 and a weak put-call ratio of 0.66.
The stock trades below its 20, 50, and 200-day moving averages, confirming strong and persistent institutional selling pressure.
Consolidated net debt remains elevated at ₹1,12,341 crore, constraining balance sheet flexibility during an energy downturn.
yudhishthira_section: ROE and ROCE figures are completely missing from the latest quarterly disclosures, leaving return on capital efficiency unverified.
Market sector headwinds are severe, with the energy sector ranking near the bottom and dropping 4.2% over the past month.
Strong telecom growth contradicts overall consolidated profit contraction, as energy segment declines outweigh digital gains.
vyasa_section: Reliance remains in a clear technical and strategic downtrend, weighed down by cyclical weakness in its core oil-to-chemicals business.
Consumer facing segments like Jio provide healthy growth, but currently lack sufficient scale to offset energy segment margin contraction.
Derivatives markets reflect dominant bearish sentiment with heavy short positioning into the November expiry.
Valuation multiples trade at a discount to historical norms, though compressed earnings justify multiple compression.
Evidence quality is constrained by undisclosed ROE and ROCE figures, warranting a cautious outlook.
levels: Immediate floor sits at the 52-week low of 1152.2, with an early breakdown indicator positioned at 1158.9.
Nearest overhead resistance aligns at 1220.8, with significant higher resistance at the 52-week peak of 1611.8.
A full upside breakout level is identified at 1334.8, above the 200-day moving average.
The stock experiences a typical daily volatility move of 29.35 points based on 14-day ATR.
watch: A sustained break below 1152.2 would mark new 52-week lows and trigger further downside momentum.
A decisive close above the 20-day SMA at 1186.41 would invalidate the dominant short-term bearish structure.
F&O call open interest shifts around the 1200 resistance and max pain strike through November expiry.
Recovery in O2C segment fuel cracks and chemical margins in upcoming earnings disclosures.

arjuna_section: Price of 1164.9 trades below 20, 50, and 200-day SMAs, confirming strong broader downward pressure near its 52-week low of 1152.2.
Trading just above the lower Bollinger band at 1146.46 indicates consolidation and compressed downside room despite prevailing weakness.
MACD at -15.64 crossing above its signal line of -16.0 reveals early positive momentum within the larger downtrend.
Above-average volume at 1.14 times normal and an ATR of 29.35 suggest active positioning with daily swings near 29.35 points.
A decisive break above the 20-day SMA at 1186.41 would invalidate the dominant bearish outlook.
chanakya_section: Reliance trades at a P/E of 19.2x to 21.4x and P/B of 1.8x to 2.7x, per Screener.in and Finology.
The current multiple is discounted against its 5-year historical average P/E of ~25.4x, reported by Screener.in.
Consolidated EV/EBITDA stands at ~22.5x, reflecting premium retail and telecom valuations over pure energy peers, per Finology.
Telecom peer Bharti Airtel trades at ~39.4x P/E, while state refiner IOCL trades at ~3.9x P/E, per Screener.in.
narada_section: Q2 FY25 consolidated net profit fell 4.8% YoY to ₹16,563 crore, primarily hurt by weak Oil-to-Chemicals margins.
Consolidated revenue stood flat at ₹2,35,481 crore, up 0.2% YoY, while EBITDA declined 2% YoY to ₹43,934 crore.
O2C segment EBITDA declined 23.7% YoY to ₹12,413 crore due to lower fuel cracks and weak chemical margins.
Jio Platforms net profit grew 23.4% YoY to ₹6,536 crore, supported by telecom tariff hikes lifting ARPU to ₹195.1.
vidura_section: Q1 FY25 gross revenue rose 11.5% YoY to ₹2,57,823 crore driven by consumer businesses, per Economic Times.
Consolidated PAT fell ~5% YoY to ₹17,448 crore as O2C fuel margins weakened, reported by Kotak Neo.
Digital Services led operational margins at 49.7%, whereas Retail delivered 8.2% EBITDA margin, according to ICICI Direct.
Consolidated net debt stood at ₹1,12,341 crore against cash reserves of ₹1,92,596 crore, per RIL's earnings release.
ROE and ROCE metrics remain unknown in the latest quarterly disclosures.

glossary.Target-before-stop odds: Out of thousands of price paths resampled from this stock's own past daily moves, how often the target was touched before the stop, the stop before the target, or neither within the window. An estimate from history, not a forecast.
glossary.Expected R: Average result in units of risk (R = entry minus stop): +0.3R means that, over many similar setups, you'd make 0.3× what you risk per trade. Paths hitting neither count as 0.
glossary.Position check: How many shares fit your own rules: risk no more than your per-trade % if the stop hits, and stay inside your single-stock, sector and cash-buffer limits.
glossary.STCG: Short-term capital gain: listed shares or equity funds sold within 12 months. Taxed at 20% (sales from 23 July 2024), plus 4% cess.
glossary.LTCG: Long-term capital gain: listed shares or equity funds held more than 12 months. The first ₹1.25 lakh a year is tax-free; the rest is taxed at 12.5% plus cess.
glossary.Tax-loss harvesting: Selling to book a loss (to offset gains) or to book long-term gains inside the yearly ₹1.25 lakh exemption, often buying back to keep the position. India has no wash-sale rule, but doing it repeatedly can draw scrutiny.
glossary.Rebalance drift: How far each holding has moved from the weight you chose for it. Past the band, the app shows the buy or sell amount that would bring it back.
glossary.Hit rate: Share of directional (Positive / Negative) calls that beat or lagged the market as called, after adjusting for the stock's beta. A coin flip scores 50%.
glossary.Edge: Average abnormal return of directional calls, counted positive when the call pointed the right way. The 95% range shows how sure we can be; a range that crosses zero means not proven.
glossary.Information coefficient: Rank correlation between the call (direction × confidence) and what happened. 0 = no link; around 0.05–0.10 is already useful in professional research.
glossary.Long\u2013short spread: How much the Positive calls outperformed the Negative calls on average — the return of buying one list and selling the other, before costs.
glossary.Brier score: How well the stated confidence matched reality, treating 70% confidence as a 70% chance of being right. 0 is perfect; 0.25 is what always saying 50% scores.
glossary.Expected move: How far the options market expects the price to travel by expiry, about one standard deviation. Roughly 2 in 3 expiries land inside this range.
glossary.Straddle: Buying the at-the-money call and put together. Its price is the market's bet on the size of the move; 85% of it is a common shortcut for the expected move.
glossary.Realised volatility: How much the price actually moved over the last 20 sessions, annualised. Compare with IV: IV above it means options are pricing more movement than recent reality.
glossary.IV rank: Where today's implied volatility sits within its own past year: 0 = lowest seen, 100 = highest. High rank favours selling options, low rank favours buying them.
glossary.Skew: Extra implied volatility on downside puts versus upside calls. A big put skew means traders are paying up for crash protection.
glossary.Fair carry: What a future should cost over spot just from interest (about 6.5% a year, pro-rated). A premium above it hints at eager longs; below it, at pressing shorts.
glossary.POP: Probability of profit: the chance, implied by option prices, that the structure ends at or above zero at expiry. Not a forecast — and higher POP usually means smaller wins than losses.
glossary.Breakeven: The expiry price where the structure neither makes nor loses money, before costs.
glossary.Bull call spread: Buy a call, sell a higher call. Small fixed cost, profit capped at the higher strike. For a moderate rise when options are not expensive.
glossary.Bull put spread: Sell a put, buy a lower put. Collect premium if the price stays above the sold strike; loss capped by the bought put. For a mild bullish view when options are rich.
glossary.Bear put spread: Buy a put, sell a lower put. Small fixed cost, profit capped at the lower strike. For a moderate fall when options are not expensive.
glossary.Bear call spread: Sell a call, buy a higher call. Collect premium if the price stays below the sold strike; loss capped by the bought call. For a mild bearish view when options are rich.
glossary.Iron condor: Sell a put and a call outside the expected range, buy further strikes as wings. Earns if price stays in the range; loss capped by the wings. For a range-bound view.
glossary.F&O bias: Net read of the futures and options signals below, from −100 (bearish) to +100 (bullish). Positioning, not a forecast.
glossary.Tailwind: Market and sector are behind this stock: its sector ranks in the top third over 1 month, the stock is beating its sector, and the market isn't risk-off. Easier to be right on a buy — still check the stock's own case.
glossary.Neutral: No strong push either way from the market or the sector. The stock's own business and chart decide.
glossary.Headwind: Market or sector is working against this stock: its sector ranks in the bottom third, or the market is risk-off and the stock lags its sector. A buy needs a strong stock-specific reason.
glossary.Unknown: Stock is outside NIFTY 200 and the sector indices tracked, so only the overall market regime applies.
glossary.Leading: Sector up over both 1 month and 1 week — strong and still strong.
glossary.Weakening: Sector up over 1 month but down this week — strength fading. Watch for a turn.
glossary.Lagging: Sector down over both 1 month and 1 week — weak and still weak.
glossary.Improving: Sector down over 1 month but up this week — early signs of a turn.
glossary.Long build-up: Futures price up and open interest up: fresh buying. Bullish positioning.
glossary.Short build-up: Futures price down and open interest up: fresh selling. Bearish positioning.
glossary.Short covering: Futures price up and open interest down: sellers exiting. Bounce, often short-lived.
glossary.Long unwinding: Futures price down and open interest down: buyers exiting. Weakening support.
glossary.PCR: Put-call ratio: open interest in puts divided by calls for the nearest expiry. Above ~1.2 = heavy put writing (traders expect support); below ~0.7 = heavy call writing (they expect a cap). Read as positioning, not a forecast.
glossary.Max pain: The expiry price at which option buyers, in total, would lose the most (and writers pay least). Prices sometimes drift toward it into expiry — weakly.
glossary.Call wall: Strike with the most call open interest — often acts as resistance this expiry.
glossary.Put wall: Strike with the most put open interest — often acts as support this expiry.
glossary.Basis: Futures price minus spot, as a % of spot. Normal is a small premium (cost of carry). A discount or a widening premium hints at positioning.
glossary.IV: Implied volatility — the yearly move option prices are pricing in. High IV = market expects big swings and options are expensive.
glossary.Regime: The market's overall mood today, from three daily checks: are most stocks rising, are most above their 50-day average, are most sectors up over a month. Risk-on = 2-3 checks pass, neutral = 1, risk-off = 0. Context, not a signal.
glossary.Breadth: How many NIFTY 200 stocks rose vs fell on the last trading day, and what share sit above their 50-day average. Broad participation makes a rally sturdier than one carried by a few heavyweights.
glossary.50-DMA: The average closing price of the last 50 trading days — a common line for the medium-term trend. Above it = uptrend, below = downtrend.
glossary.Sector strength: Sector indices ranked by 1-month return. Money tends to keep flowing to leading sectors for a while; a stock in a top sector has the wind behind it.
glossary.OI build-up: From stock futures: price change plus change in open interest (open contracts). Price up + OI up = long build-up (fresh buying). Price down + OI up = short build-up (fresh selling). Price up + OI down = short covering. Price down + OI down = long unwinding. Shows positioning, not a forecast.
glossary.Stock in context: One stock checked against the day's regime, its sector's rank and whether it is beating its sector. Tailwind / Neutral / Headwind. Also handed to the final-report writer as one line.
glossary.NIFTY 1M: NIFTY 50's return over roughly the last 21 trading days — the benchmark for the sector table. Sectors above it are leading the market.
glossary.P/E: Investors are paying this many rupees for every ₹1 the company earns in a year. High can mean expected growth, or an expensive price — it depends on the company.
glossary.P/B: The price compared to what the company's assets are worth on paper.
glossary.ROE: How much profit the company makes from the money shareholders put in. Higher is better.
glossary.ROCE: How well the company turns all its capital — including borrowed money — into profit.
glossary.EPS: The company's yearly profit divided across each share.
glossary.EV/EBITDA: The whole company's value compared to its operating earnings. Used to compare companies that carry different amounts of debt.
glossary.CAGR: The steady yearly rate that would have taken you from the starting value to today's.
glossary.RSI: A 0-100 momentum gauge. Above 70 means the price has run up fast; below 30 means it has fallen fast. Neither is a buy or sell signal on its own.
glossary.MACD: Compares a short-term and a long-term price average. Crossing above suggests momentum is turning up, below that it is turning down.
glossary.ATR: How much the price typically moves in a single day. A measure of choppiness.
glossary.AUM: The total money investors have put into this fund.
glossary.Expense Ratio: The yearly fee the fund charges, as a percentage of your money. It is already taken out of the NAV you see.
glossary.NAV: The per-unit price of the fund, updated at the end of each trading day.
glossary.Benchmark: The index the fund is trying to beat. Returns mean little without it.
glossary.Max Drawdown: The worst peak-to-bottom fall in the past. What a bad stretch has felt like.
glossary.Sharpe Ratio: Return earned per unit of bumpiness. Higher means a smoother ride for the same result.
glossary.Alpha: Return above what the benchmark delivered — the part credited to the manager.
glossary.Beta: How much the fund moves when the market moves. Above 1 swings harder than the market.
glossary.52-week range: The highest and lowest the price has been over the past year.
glossary.Exit Load: A fee charged if you sell your units before a set holding period.
glossary.DMA: Daily Moving Average. The average closing price over a chosen number of trading sessions. A 50 DMA uses the last 50 sessions; a 200 DMA shows the longer-term trend.
glossary.SMA: Simple Moving Average. The average closing price over a fixed number of trading sessions, with every session weighted equally.
glossary.EMA: Exponential Moving Average. A moving average that gives more weight to recent prices, so it reacts faster than an SMA.
glossary.WMA: Weighted Moving Average. A moving average that gives greater weight to selected recent prices than older prices.
glossary.HMA: Hull Moving Average. A smoother, faster-reacting moving average designed to reduce lag while keeping price noise lower.
glossary.Stochastic RSI: A momentum indicator that applies the Stochastic calculation to RSI. It moves quickly between 0 and 100 and can flag short-term momentum extremes.
glossary.CCI: Commodity Channel Index. Measures how far price is from its recent average. Extreme positive or negative readings can indicate unusually strong momentum.
glossary.Rate of change: The percentage change in price over a chosen lookback period. It shows how quickly price momentum is changing.
glossary.Williams %R: A 0 to -100 momentum oscillator showing where the latest close sits within the recent high-low range. Readings near 0 indicate strong recent closes; near -100 indicate weak ones.
glossary.Momentum: The change in price over a chosen number of sessions. Positive momentum means price is above its earlier level; negative means it is below.
glossary.BB width: Bollinger Band Width. Measures the distance between the upper and lower Bollinger Bands. Narrow bands mean low recent volatility; widening bands mean volatility is increasing.
glossary.Keltner Channels: Volatility bands around an exponential moving average, typically based on ATR. They help show trend direction and unusually strong price moves.
glossary.Donchian Channels: Bands formed from the highest high and lowest low over a chosen lookback period. Breaks above or below them highlight new range extremes.
glossary.Historical volatility: A measure of how much returns have varied over a past period. Higher historical volatility means larger price swings.
glossary.Volume: The number of shares or units traded during the period. Higher volume can make a price move more meaningful and easier to trade.
glossary.Relative volume: Current volume compared with its typical volume. Above 1 means more volume than usual; below 1 means less.
glossary.Accumulation/Distribution: A volume-based indicator that combines price location within the day's range with volume to estimate buying or selling pressure.
glossary.Parabolic SAR: A trailing trend indicator that places dots above or below price. It can help identify trend direction and possible trailing-stop levels.
glossary.PE: Same as P/E: the price investors pay for each ₹1 of annual company earnings. It is useful only when compared with growth, quality and peers.
glossary.ADX: Average Directional Index. Measures how strong a trend is, not which way it points. Above 25 means a real trend; below that, moving-average signals are mostly noise.
glossary.Bollinger Bands: A 20-day average with bands two standard deviations either side. Price outside a band is unusual for that stock, not necessarily wrong.
glossary.VWAP: Volume Weighted Average Price. The average price paid, weighted by how much traded at each level. On daily bars this is a rolling 50-day figure, not a session VWAP.
glossary.Supertrend: A trailing line that flips between long and short based on ATR. Simple, and late at turning points by design.
glossary.Ichimoku: A Japanese system whose 'cloud' marks a support and resistance band projected forward. Price above the cloud is bullish, below is bearish, inside is unclear.
glossary.OBV: On-Balance Volume. Adds volume on up days and subtracts it on down days. Rising OBV with flat price suggests accumulation.
glossary.MFI: Money Flow Index. RSI weighted by volume, so it reacts to conviction as well as direction. Below 20 is oversold, above 80 overbought.
glossary.CMF: Chaikin Money Flow. Positive means buying pressure closed the day near the highs on decent volume; negative is the reverse.
glossary.Stochastic: Where today's close sits within the recent high-low range, 0 to 100. Measures position in the range, not trend.
glossary.Swing high / low: A price peak or trough with lower highs (or higher lows) either side. Where the market actually turned, rather than a round number.
glossary.Breakout: A close above the highest close of the prior 60 sessions. Confirmed only when two of the last three closes, today's included, are above it on volume at least 1.5x average — a wick through a level is not a breakout.
glossary.Entry zone: Support up to 0.75 ATR above it. If price is already above this, the zone is a level to wait for, not a signal today.
glossary.Stop: The exit price if the reading is wrong. Placed 0.75 ATR below support so an ordinary day's noise does not reach it.
glossary.Risk / reward: Reward to the first target divided by risk to the stop, measured from what you would pay today rather than a stale entry price.
glossary.R multiple: A trade's result in units of the risk taken. Losing at the stop is -1R; making twice the risk is +2R.
glossary.Win rate: Share of trades that finished profitable after costs. A low win rate is fine if the winners are much larger than the losers.
glossary.Profit factor: Gross profit divided by gross loss. Above 1 means the strategy made money; below 1 means it lost.
glossary.Expectancy: Average result per trade after costs. The number that actually compounds.
glossary.MAE: Maximum Adverse Excursion. The worst a trade went against you before it finished. If winners routinely take heat near the stop, the stop is too tight.
glossary.MFE: Maximum Favourable Excursion. The best a trade looked before it finished. Large values on losing trades suggest targets are set too far away.
glossary.Walk-forward: Testing across consecutive chronological slices instead of one lump. A strategy that only works in some periods shows up here.
glossary.Out of sample: Results on data held back from the design. The honest test — in-sample numbers can always be made to look good.
glossary.Parameter sensitivity: Re-running with different settings. A result that survives across several is robust; one that works at a single value was fitted.
glossary.Sortino Ratio: Like Sharpe but penalising only downside moves. Inflates when losses cluster at a fixed stop, so read Sharpe alongside it.
glossary.Confidence: How much the signals agree, 5 to 95. Not a probability, and not a forecast. A bearish chart with everything aligned scores high.
glossary.NO TRADE: There is no setup worth acting on. A valid answer, and the most common one.
glossary.Screener: Every stock in the universe run through the same rules as a stock's Setup tab. Buy now = passes every rule; Wait = valid setup but price has run above the entry zone. Price and volume only — fundamentals need a full research run.
glossary.Young listing: Listed on NSE within the last year. Judged on fewer checks (no 200-day average, monthly trend or backtest), blocked below its listing price, grade capped at B.
glossary.WAIT: The setup is valid but price has already run above the entry zone, so buying now risks too much for the reward. Worth acting on only if price pulls back into the zone.
glossary.Invalidation: The price at which the reading is wrong. Decide this before acting.
glossary.Relative strength: Return minus the index return. A stock rising less than NIFTY is still underperforming.
glossary.Liquidity: Daily traded value. Thin liquidity means your own order moves the price.
glossary.Consensus zone: Where several independent target projections cluster. A range is honest where a single number would be false precision.
glossary.XIRR: The yearly return on money paid in at different times — the honest number for a monthly SIP, where a plain CAGR would assume you invested it all on day one.
glossary.SIP: Investing a fixed amount every month rather than a lump sum. Buys more units when the price is low and fewer when it is high.
glossary.Rolling returns: The return of every possible window of a given length, not just the latest one. Shows the range of outcomes rather than one lucky start date.
glossary.Split: A company dividing each share into several cheaper ones. The price falls in proportion — nothing is lost, but unadjusted price history looks like a crash.
